name: the meadows
title: Open Meadows
description: Beyond the cliff stretches a succession of open meadows, their tall grasses undulating beneath the wind. The sea is hidden behind the rising ground.
A broad tract of grassland extends towards the next hill, broken only by low bushes. The cliffs have concealed the ocean from view.
Grasses rise almost to the waist in places, their pale heads bending in long waves. From beyond the cliff comes only the distant murmur of the sea.
_map: position on the route map (grid cells); the camp (travelHours 0) has a path to every place

log: Scattered bushes interrupt the grassy slope; farther down, a belt of willows suggests the presence of water.
Beyond the nearer shrubs, willows stand in a shallow depression where a stream or river may run.
Dark bushes mark the meadow here and there. Lower on the slope a line of willows demands closer examination.

_arrive: what you see each time you come back: every line whose 'when' holds, in order

text: The open meadows spread once more beneath the wind.
You return to the tall grass, which bends in broad waves across the slope.
The country opens before you, bright and spacious after the narrow cliff path.
Here the sky is unconfined, and grasses brush against your knees.
Night leaves the meadow without visible boundaries; the grass whispers about your legs.
In the darkness you distinguish the movement of grass more by sound than sight.
The meadow is dark beneath the stars, and insects call from somewhere among the stems.
The berry bushes remain laden with ripe fruit.
Dark fruit still hangs in clusters upon the bushes.
The shrubs continue to offer a considerable supply of berries.
Below the meadow the river follows its course between the willows.
The murmur of the river reaches you before its water comes into view.
The river still runs clear and swift beneath the trees.
The ears of corn have ripened in your cultivated field.
The planted corn stands tall, its ears heavy and ready for harvest.

explore._explore: look around: a pop-up with what you see (view lines whose 'when' holds) and the landmarks not explored yet; no time passes until you pick one

text: Tall grass extends inland over gently rising ground, its surface stirred into waves by the wind.
From here the meadow reaches the next low hill without interruption.
The grasses move in pale green and silver bands across the open country.

view.text: Several dark shrubs break the otherwise continuous expanse of grass.
The bushes you examined are heavy with dark, ripe fruit.
Lower on the slope the crowns of willows form a narrow line.
The river runs beneath the willows, its water broken by stones.
Near the river lies a level tract where the grass grows unusually thick.
Among the grasses stand a few taller stems bearing conspicuous seed heads.
Beyond the bushes a steady humming rises from the flowers.

nothingLeft: The open ground presents no new feature, only grass bending before the wind.
By now you have examined the principal resources of these meadows.
Your survey of the grassy slope reveals nothing further today.

landmarks.label: the bushes
text: A closer inspection reveals that the shrubs are laden with small, almost black berries. Their first taste is sharp, but sweetness follows; here is food requiring little preparation.
The dark fruit proves soft and ripe. You sample a berry and find it tart but wholesome, promising a useful addition to your provisions.
Hundreds of berries hang among the leaves. Though small and rather sour at first, they are edible and may readily be gathered.
landmarks.journal: You find edible berries among the shrubs.

landmarks.label: the willows
text: Beneath the willows you discover a river running clear over a bed of stones. Its water is fresh; in the quieter pools, fish hold their position against the current and might be taken with a spear.
The line of willows conceals a brisk river. Its cold water is fit to drink, and fish can be seen waiting in the sheltered bends, within reach of a careful spear thrust.
A stream of considerable size flows beneath the trees, swift in its shallows and quiet in its deeper turns. It promises both drinking water and fish, if proper tools can be made.
landmarks.journal: You discover a river, with fresh water and fish.

landmarks.label: the flat ground
text: Near the river you find a stretch of level ground with a dark, friable soil. With a hoe to break the turf, it might be converted into a productive field.
The grass here conceals unusually deep and fertile earth. The proximity of water makes this an excellent site for cultivation, once the ground can be turned.
A small plain beside the river offers the two chief requirements of a field: workable soil and ready water. It remains only to fashion a suitable hoe.
landmarks.journal: You find fertile, level ground beside the river.

landmarks.label: the tall seed heads
text: Among the grasses you recognise a patch of wild corn, whose slender ears hold edible grain. The kernels might be consumed now, or reserved for sowing.
Several taller stalks bear the unmistakable ears of corn, though the grain is small. Thus the meadow offers not only present nourishment but the possibility of a future crop.
You discover wild corn growing between the grasses. Its ears are modest, yet they provide both food and, more importantly, seed.
landmarks.journal: Wild corn offers food now and seed for planting.

landmarks.label: the humming
text: Following the hum, you find wild bees visiting a bank of flowers. If a hollow log could be offered as shelter, a colony might be established and its honey collected.
The flowers are alive with bees, whose movements suggest a nest nearby. A suitable hollow log could perhaps persuade them to remain within easy reach.
Hundreds of bees work among the blossoms. Their presence suggests a new resource: a managed hive, and in time a supply of honey.
landmarks.journal: Wild bees visit the flowers. A hive may attract them.

activities.name: pick berries
log: The fruit stains your fingers a deep purple.
You gather the berries steadily, examining one branch after another.
The thorns catch upon your sleeves as you collect the small fruit.
You fill your hands and pockets with the berries growing here.
You select the dark, ripe berries carefully to avoid bruising them.

activities.name: drink water
log: You kneel at the riverbank and drink the clear, sweet water.
The fresh water is cold enough to set your teeth aching.
You drink from your cupped hands while the current runs between your fingers.
The river water carries a faint taste of stone and grasses.

activities.name: catch fish

text: Two fish are taken from the pool, and lie struggling in the grass.
The same quiet reach of river yields two useful fish.
You secure two silver fish, a satisfactory return for your patience.
One fish rewards your labour in the river.
You draw one struggling fish out of the water.
Your spear takes a single fish, surprisingly heavy for its size.
The current carries the disturbed fish beyond your reach.
At the first movement the fish vanish into deeper water.
The spear rises bearing nothing but a strand of river weed.

log: You take your position on a stone above the pool and wait with spear raised.
You wade knee-deep into the current, seeking a fish that holds still.
In the shade of the willows, you wait for the proper moment to strike.

activities.name: cut willow twigs
log: You cut a bundle of long, flexible shoots from the willows.
The fresh willow twigs bend readily without breaking, an excellent property for weaving.
You collect slender willow branches, chosen for their length and suppleness.

activities.name: gather corn
log: You search the taller grasses for the seed heads of wild corn.
Several slender ears of corn reward your search.
The wild corn bears small ears filled with hard, usable grain.
